title: onprem: airgap offline bundle + vendoring for rke2 (Ubuntu 22.04) + apt-mirror tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: customers running Redwood Private in air-gapped/on-prem environments have requested first-class support for RKE2 on Ubuntu 22.04, plus more robust tooling for building offline bundles and hosting apt mirrors. This PR implements vendoring updates and an automated apt-mirror toolchain that produces fully offline-installable bundles, improves package reproducibility, and adds rollback/verification hooks for upgrades. Motivation: several enterprise customers required Ubuntu 22.04 images (kernel and libc constraints) and ability to import the full offline bundle into internal registries/apt mirrors. Previously we relied on distro-agnostic tarballs which caused missing .deb dependencies and kernel module mismatches on Ubuntu variants. What this PR does (summary): - Add rke2/ubuntu-22.04 offline bundle manifests and vendor pipeline changes that pin package versions and include TUF metadata for integrity checks. - New apt-mirror generation module (installer/tools/apt-mirror) that pulls, signs, and packages apt repositories into an airgap bundle; supports GPG signing and optional timestamping for TUF metadata. - Terraform module updates for onprem deployments to optionally configure a local apt mirror service and reference vendored artifact paths. - Helm chart tweaks to ensure nodeSelector/taints compatible with RKE2 single-node and HA clusters on Ubuntu 22.04. - Upgrade/rollback: add post-install verification job and basic rollback helper scripts (installer/upgrade/verify.sh, installer/upgrade/rollback.sh) that validate kernel/module compatibility and resume previous config on failure. - CI and release metadata: add smoke tests in the perf-canary harness to validate bundle unpack + dry-run install in a containerized simulation. Checklist: - [x] Offline bundle manifests for rke2/ubuntu-22.04 - [x] Apt-mirror generator and packaging script - [x] Vendored .deb list and TUF metadata - [x] Helm chart compatibility fixes - [x] Terraform module knobs for apt mirror - [x] Unit tests for apt-mirror tool and verification job - [x] Release notes entry Commits (high level): - 1/7: feat(installer): add apt-mirror tool and packaging pipeline - 2/7: feat(installer): offline bundle manifest for rke2/ubuntu-22.04 - 3/7: chore(vendor): pin deb versions and add TUF metadata generation - 4/7: feat(terraform): add apt_mirror module + examples - 5/7: fix(chart): rke2 nodeSelector/taint handling for ubuntu-22.04 - 6/7: feat(upgrade): add verify.sh and rollback.sh helpers - 7/7: test(ci): add smoke test scenario for airgap bundle install Simulation / testing notes: I ran the apt-mirror generator against the Ubuntu 22.04 focal-derivative mirror (mirror snapshot), produced a ~1.2GB bundle (gzipped) containing the minimal package set we need for RKE2 + containerd + kernel headers, and validated the bundle installs in a containerized chroot that mimics installer behavior. The TUF metadata was validated with the python-tuf client. Files changed (high-level): - installer/offline-bundles/rke2/ubuntu-22.04/manifest.yaml - installer/tools/apt-mirror/generate_mirror.py - installer/tools/apt-mirror/packager.sh - vendor/debs/ubuntu-22.04/ (pinned list + hashes) - terraform/modules/onprem/apt_mirror/main.tf - helm-charts/redwood/templates/node-affinity.yaml - installer/upgrade/verify.sh - installer/upgrade/rollback.sh - ci/perf-canary/airgap-smoke.yml - docs/onprem/airgap.md (usage and troubleshooting) Security & reproducibility: vendoring includes SHA256 hashes and TUF delegations to ensure artifacts are tamper-evident. Apt-mirror generation runs in a hermetic container with ephemeral keys for signing; we document how to replace keys with customer KMS/HSM. Backwards compatibility: default installer behavior is unchanged unless the new apt_mirror terraform option is enabled. Helm changes are additive and guarded by feature flags to avoid affecting existing clusters. Rollout plan: merge to main -> cut release candidate build containing offline bundles -> test with QA's onprem lab (internal) -> notify customers in the PM ticket for early adopters. Release notes: add entry under Private Installer - Ubuntu 22.04 RKE2: airgap bundle and apt-mirror tooling, vendored packages + rollback tooling. Known limitations: - Bundle size can be large (1-2GB) depending on selected package set; the apt-mirror tool supports filters to reduce footprint. - Does not yet support older Debian derivatives (follow-up PR planned). Related: ENG-2019 (RKE2 22.04 support), PM-1348 (customer request for apt mirror).

Jenna Park: Please add a smoke test that validates GPG signature verification after unpack — otherwise rollback detection may be blind.
